landing.faq.a1: AKIS connects to your GitHub, Jira, and Confluence accounts via OAuth. It monitors your repositories and issue trackers, running agents automatically based on your configured triggers.
landing.faq.a2: Absolutely. AKIS is SOC 2 compliant with end-to-end encryption. Your code is processed in isolated environments and never stored permanently. Enterprise customers can opt for self-hosted deployments.
landing.faq.a3: Yes! Agents are configured through YAML playbooks that define triggers, behaviors, and output destinations. You can customize everything from documentation style to test frameworks.
landing.faq.a4: All agent outputs are reviewable before publishing. You can set up approval workflows, and every action is logged with full transparency. You're always in control.
landing.faq.a5: Teams typically save 20+ hours per week on documentation, testing, and prototyping tasks. The exact savings depend on your team size and workflow complexity.
landing.faq.a6: Yes! Our Starter plan is completely free and includes 1 agent and 100 jobs per month. Perfect for solo developers and small teams getting started.

tech.mlx.label: MLX & Quantization
tech.mlx.headline: Local AI, Maximum Performance
tech.mlx.description: Apple's MLX framework unlocks the full potential of Apple Silicon's unified memory architecture for LLM inference — delivering speeds that rival cloud APIs.
tech.mlx.unified.title: Unified Memory Architecture
tech.mlx.unified.body: Unlike traditional GPUs, Apple Silicon shares RAM between CPU and GPU. This means no data copying overhead — a 32B parameter model can run in 18GB of shared memory, achieving 2x the speed of PyTorch on the same hardware.
tech.mlx.quant.title: 4-bit Quantization
tech.mlx.quant.body: Quantization compresses model weights from 32-bit floats to 4-bit integers — reducing memory by 8x with only 2-5% quality loss. This allows running 32 billion parameter models on a laptop with 24GB RAM.
tech.mlx.benchmark.title: MLX Benchmark — Apple M4 Pro 24GB
tech.mlx.benchmark.note: Measured on Apple M4 Pro 24GB Unified Memory, February 2026. MLX achieves 50-100% faster inference than Ollama/llama.cpp on the same hardware.

docsPage.sections.gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
docsPage.sections.gettingStarted.content:
## Getting Started

### Creating an Account
1. Click the **"Get Started"** button on the homepage
2. Enter your email address or sign in with GitHub/Google
3. Complete email verification

### Setting Up an AI Provider
1. After signing in, go to the **Settings** page
2. Click the **"+ Add"** button next to the AI provider you want to use
3. Enter your API key and save
4. Select your default provider

### Connecting GitHub
A GitHub connection is required for the Proto agent to generate and push code:
- If you signed in with GitHub OAuth, it connects automatically
- Alternative: Add a Personal Access Token from Settings > GitHub
docsPage.sections.pipeline.title: Pipeline Flow
docsPage.sections.pipeline.content:
## Pipeline Flow

AKIS's 3-stage pipeline transforms your idea into working code:

### 1. Scribe — Spec Creation
- Start a new chat and describe your project
- The Scribe agent asks questions to clarify your idea
- Produces a structured spec (feature document)
- Review and **approve** the spec, or edit and resubmit

### 2. Proto — Code Generation
- Creates an MVP scaffold based on the approved spec
- Pushes files to GitHub (branch: `proto/scaffold-{timestamp}`)
- Supported stacks: React+Vite, Next.js, Node.js+Express, Python+FastAPI

### 3. Trace — Test Generation
- Reads the code produced by Proto from GitHub
- Writes Playwright e2e tests specific to that code
- Commits tests to the same branch

### State Machine
```
scribe_clarifying → scribe_generating → awaiting_approval
→ proto_building → trace_testing → completed
```
docsPage.sections.providers.title: AI Providers
docsPage.sections.providers.content:
## AI Providers

AKIS supports three different AI providers:

### Anthropic (Claude)
- **Default model:** claude-sonnet-4-6
- **Get API Key:** [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/)
- Key format: `sk-ant-...`

### OpenAI
- **Default model:** gpt-4o
- **Get API Key:** [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/)
- Key format: `sk-...`

### OpenRouter
- **Default model:** anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
- **Get API Key:** [openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai/)
- Key format: `sk-or-...`
- Access multiple models with a single key
- Free models available (e.g., google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free)
docsPage.sections.settings.title: Settings
docsPage.sections.settings.content:
## Settings

### API Key Management
- You can add a separate key for each provider
- Keys are encrypted and stored using AES-256-GCM
- You can select your default provider
- You can update or delete keys at any time

### GitHub Connection
- If you signed in with OAuth, it is automatically connected
- You can check the connection status on the Settings page
docsPage.sections.faq.title: FAQ
docsPage.sections.faq.content:
## Frequently Asked Questions

### How long does a pipeline take?
A typical pipeline takes 2-5 minutes. Complex projects may take longer.

### Which languages are supported?
Spec writing can be in Turkish or English. Code generation is based on the project's stack.

### Can I use it for free?
Yes! You can use free models via OpenRouter. Simply add your OpenRouter key from Settings and select a free model.

### Can I edit the spec?
Yes, after Scribe generates the spec you can click "Reject" to make edits and resubmit.

### Can it push to my existing repo?
Yes, the Proto agent can push to an existing repo by opening a new branch.
